messages:
sam.w: quick heads-up — onboarding marlin9b with our int4 exporter. seeing a repeating 'zipper' artifact in embedding PCA and cosine heatmaps after quant. small repro below. :eyes:

sam.w: repro steps:
```
# on bench VM
git checkout onboard/marlin
python tools/run_eval.py --model marlin9b --quant int4 --seq 512 --batch 1 --dump-embeds=1 --seed 42
```

sam.w: short numbers: float16 top1 0.785, int8 0.778, int4 0.613; embed cosine mean f16 vs int4 = 0.66. pattern shows alternating head groups with phase flips — looks like a zipper across positions 128,256,384.

anya: can you paste export flags (exact)? which rotary flag (headwise/shared)? any LN-fold or proj packing? tokenizers?

sam.w: exporter: `rdw-quant-v2 --mode int4 --scheme sym-clamp --proj-order packed-qkv` ; kept rotary default (shared). no ln-fold. tokenizer: bpe-nfkc-v2025.

ciro: that packed-qkv + shared-rotary smell like cross-head scale mixing. when q/k are packed, scale heterogeneity can cause quantizer to clip unevenly and create phase aliasing. try `rotary.headwise=true` and unpack qkv ordering.

maya: also try `rotary.freq_scale=0.98` and `freq_scale=1.02` — small shifts sometimes push phase out of a wrap boundary. and compare int8->int4 delta to see if it's monotonic.

sam.w: quick tokenizer sanity: `tokenizer.encode("Hello world!")` identical across float and int builds. so not token mismatch.

bench-bot: job 1719012350 finished, results stored at s3://redwood-qa/marlin/onboard/1719012350/ (logs + embeds).

eva: another thing — KV warmup + batch accumulation can amplify steady-state rotatory error. try `--kv-warmup 0` vs `--kv-warmup 128` and a run with `--batch 1 --no-batch-accum` to see if zipper correlates with cache reuse.

ciro: micro-plan: re-export matrix {rotary.headwise: true,false} x {proj-order: packed-qkv, qkv-serial} x {ln-fold: true,false} x {freq_scale: 0.98,1.0,1.02}. measure per-head embed cosine and per-head rotary matrix diffs.

sam.w: starting that grid now. first run (headwise + qkv-serial + ln-fold=false + freq_scale=1.0): int4 top1 improved to 0.71, embed cosine mean=0.79. zipper amplitude reduced but still visible at seq>1024.

maya: improvement is significant — suggests proj packing and shared rotary were amplifying quant noise. for residual longctx effect, check that our converter didn't accidentally tile the 1D freq vector into heads instead of proper per-head broadcast (we had that bug on an earlier model).

eva: if you still see residuals, dump raw rotary cos/sin tables for head 0..15 float16 vs int4 and compute phase offset per position. if quantizer saturates some sin values, we might need per-head clipping or asymmetric-biased quant.

sam.w: noted. i'll dump per-head rotaries + embed PCA snapshots and attach links when done. thanks all, will post plots here. :thumbsup:
